meta.rule: Every signal was declared before it was scored. Signals that fail are published with their effect size, because the failures are the useful output.

signals.name: Own-line spread edge
signals.tested: Model home margin minus the closing spread, either side, at 1.5 and 3.0 point thresholds
signals.why_it_should_work: If the opponent-adjusted ratings carry information the market has not priced, the disagreement should predict the margin.
signals.why_not: The model's own spread error is larger than the market's (10.40 vs 9.72 points in 2025), so its disagreements are mostly its own noise.

signals.name: Own-total edge
signals.tested: Model total minus the closing total at 2.5 and 4.0 point thresholds
signals.why_it_should_work: Totals are less efficiently priced than sides in some markets, so a ratings-based total could carry information.
signals.why_not: Both are positive but neither survives correction, and both are negative in the 2024-2025 holdout.

signals.name: Rest differential
signals.tested: Bet the side with 3+ more rest days
signals.why_it_should_work: A short week is a documented recovery cost.
signals.why_not: Effect size indistinguishable from zero over the largest sample on the board.

signals.name: Divisional road underdog
signals.why_it_should_work: Familiarity compresses margins in division games.
signals.why_not: Negative point estimate; the familiarity story did not show up in the price.

signals.name: Fade the road favourite
signals.tested: Home side when the visitor is favoured by 7+
signals.why_it_should_work: Large road favourites are a well-known public-bias target.
signals.why_not: Twelve rules were tested; p=0.198 does not survive Benjamini-Hochberg, and a 44-bet holdout cannot confirm 6%.

signals.name: Home off a bye
signals.tested: Home team with 13+ rest days against a visitor with fewer
signals.why_not: Negative; also the smallest sample on the board, so it cannot rule out a small effect either way.

signals.name: Extreme totals
signals.tested: Under when the closing total is 40 or lower; over when it is 50 or higher
signals.why_it_should_work: Totals at the extremes may be over-adjusted by the market.
signals.why_not: The under rule is the only rule on the board whose raw p-value clears 0.05, and it clears it in the wrong direction.

signals.name: Opponent quarterback out
signals.tested: Bet against a side whose QB is ruled Out or Doubtful
signals.why_it_should_work: A backup quarterback is a large, publicly known downgrade — the market should already price it, and the test is whether it over- or under-prices.
signals.why_not: The market appears to price the downgrade fully; there is no residual edge in the direction tested.

signals.name: Injury-count gap
signals.tested: Bet against the side with 3+ more players ruled Out
signals.why_not: A count of 'Out' players is a poor measure of lost value: it ignores who the player is, which is exactly what the depth-chart work is meant to fix.

signals.name: Closing-line correlation
signals.tested: Pearson r between the closing spread and the actual home margin
signals.why_it_should_work: Not a strategy — the benchmark any own line has to beat.
signals.why_not: An own line beating the market must correlate with the margin better than this; the current model correlates 0.345.

signals.name: Parlay leg dependence
signals.tested: 66 two-leg combinations, correlation ratio against independence, BH-corrected
signals.why_it_should_work: Standard parlays are priced at the product of the legs, which is only fair if the legs are independent.
signals.why_not: A positive return on a correlated pair is the book's multiplication rule, not a forecast. A book that prices same-game correlation would remove it.

signals.name: Player props
signals.tested: Usage-based projections for passing, rushing and receiving markets
signals.why_it_should_work: Shrunk usage projections can beat a naive per-game average.
signals.result: no price, so no bet scored
signals.why_not: No prop price exists in any source in this repository, so a prop ROI would be invented. Projections are published; results are not.
